title: Projection curve is a true 1/range perspective divide in both ROM and clone
claim: ROM formula: screen_x = lateral/range and screen_y = height/range — the Math Box divides the rotated lateral coord by range for the horizontal, and the hardware Z-divider (ZDIV, fed the vertex height via DDEND in PNTPUT) divides the vertical by the same range; both screen axes are proportional to 1/range. Clone formula: perspective(fovY,...) 4x4 matrix followed by the w-divide in transform(), giving screen ∝ 1/z_eye. Same curve (hyperbolic 1/z), not linear/orthographic.
reasoning: PNTPUT loads each vertex's 3rd word (height) into DDEND, KLUDGE moves it to DIVOUT and `STA ZDIV` starts the divide (BZONE.MAC:2121); the first Math Box read is the range used for the horizontal divide and the near/far test (BZONE.MAC:1698-1700). Clone: scene.ts:66 builds a standard perspective matrix and scene.ts:111 applies it with a perspective divide. The near/far cull constants themselves (NEAR_CULL 1023, FAR_CULL 31487) come from the clone's mathbox.html doc (non-shipped, uncitable); the shipped far-cull evidence is `CMP I,7B` on the doubled range high byte (BZONE.MAC:1699).

title: Horizontal field of view: ROM's +-45deg (90deg full) cull cone equals the clone's 90deg DISPLAY_FOV
claim: ROM ROTPNT discards any object whose |lateral| >= range (BZONE.MAC:1719-1723: `LDA Y1 / CMP X2 / LDA Y1+1 / SBC X2+1 / BCS discard`, where X2=range and Y1=|lateral|). |lateral| < range means half-angle < atan(1) = 45deg, i.e. a 90deg FULL horizontal cone. The clone renders DISPLAY_FOV = 2*H_FOV = 2*(PI/4) = PI/2 = 90deg full horizontal field (camera.ts:57, scene.ts:65) — matching the ROM cone. Objects beyond +-45deg fall outside NDC +-1 and are clipped, so the clone reproduces the angular cull via projection clipping rather than an explicit per-object test.
reasoning: The clone's H_FOV=PI/4 is really the HALF-angle of this cone; the comment framing it as 'the 45deg VISIBILITY cone' and DISPLAY_FOV as 'deliberately WIDER' (camera.ts:46-57) mischaracterizes the geometry (90deg is the full cone, not a widening), but the rendered field (90deg full) is the correct match. The clone's explicit cull (scene.ts:75-80) is distance-only; the angular cull is achieved by NDC clipping, which is behaviorally equivalent for on/off-screen visibility.

title: Trig: ROM uses a fixed-point Q15 quarter-wave SIN table + 2-step EXTRAPOLATE; clone uses IEEE-754 float
claim: ROM SIN/COS is a 65-entry quarter-wave lookup in Q15 fixed point: table runs 0x0000, 0x0324, 0x0647 ... 0x7FFF (0x7FFF = amplitude 1.0), indexed by an 8-bit angle (256 steps = full circle), with COS(a)=SIN(a+0x40) and sign/quadrant folding. EXTRAPOLATE (SINXTR/COSXTR) linearly interpolates 2 sub-divisions between adjacent table entries for finer landscape rotation. The clone instead calls IEEE-754 Math.sin/Math.cos (camera.ts:64, and math3d rotationY) at full float precision, with only the input orientation quantized to the 8-bit wheel.
reasoning: SIN table BZONE.MAC:2174-2190 (65 `.WORD`s, HEX); routine header BZONE.MAC:2138-2145; EXTRAPOLATE BZONE.MAC:2192-2247. EXTRAPOLATE is invoked only for the landscape angle LANGLE (BZONE.MAC:1473-1490) which drives the mountain/horizon (out of the object pair's scope, handled by horizon.ts); the OBJECT pipeline (PNTPUT, BZONE.MAC:2002-2014) calls SIN/COS directly with no extrapolation. This is a deterministic float-vs-fixed representational difference, not a value error: the clone is strictly more precise. Accept; note the ROM's 1/256 orientation quantization is preserved by the clone's facing-byte inputs (see W-013).
